title: Causal appraisal of asphalt pavement field experiments: warm mix asphalt and rehabilitation policies
stage: Frozen after independent scientific review and before new control fits; not prospective registration

controls.stationary-rounded: Same bounded latent interval likelihood as event-rounded; event_kernel=0, all other priors/mean/104records/13target campaigns unchanged
controls.calendar-matched: Same linear mean and2 independent Beta(2,2) attenuation parameters. Preserve observed min-to-max jump count separately for each road/counter. For n_j jumps use fractions k/(n_j+1) plus/minus1/[8*(nC+nS+1)] of each road observed-age range. No Y or actual operation dates choose cuts.

parameter_count: Calendar/event both have ell,sigma_process,sigma_visit and2 attenuation parameters; per-road/counter total jumps and prior cumulative attenuation over observed span are matched. Pairwise covariance geometry can differ; no unique physical mechanism inferred.
validation: Same52 conditional physical-pair deletions, k<=.7 AND weightESS>=400 else exact same-prior refit; use bin mass for rounded likelihood
comparison_scope: Test kernel benefit under a shared recording likelihood, and a clock-only equally parameterized alternative; report all outcomes even if event advantage disappears.
interval_invariance: Move each actual operation inside its same observed-survey interval, retaining multiplicity; the event-count matrix and all52 tasks then have identical kernel law. This is a model-resolution property, not a causal timing claim.
